The community groups come from the **microbiome species table** (same definition
as notebook 02): the fraction of reads that belong to *Lactobacillus*, split at
0.5. The gene table is then tested against those groups with DESeq2. That keeps
the workshop rule intact: the group is defined from one table and tested on the
other.

Positive log2 fold change will mean **higher expression in `lactobacillus`
samples**. We check the direction explicitly at the end.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)

data_dir <- "data/2-workshop2/group_b_contraception"

metadata <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "01_metadata.csv"))
species_counts <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "02_microbiome_counts.csv"))
taxonomy <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "03_microbiome_taxonomy.csv"))
gene_counts <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "04_rnaseq_counts.csv.gz"))
```

## Step 1: define community from the microbiome table

```{r}
# Lactobacillus fraction per sample: Lactobacillus reads / all reads.
# In this file the taxa are ROWS and the samples are columns.
lacto_taxa <- taxonomy$taxon[taxonomy$Genus == "Lactobacillus"]
counts_only <- as.matrix(species_counts[-1])          # drop the taxon column
storage.mode(counts_only) <- "numeric"
lacto_rows <- species_counts[[1]] %in% lacto_taxa

sample_groups <- tibble(
  sample_id      = colnames(counts_only),
  total_reads    = colSums(counts_only),
  lacto_reads    = colSums(counts_only[lacto_rows, , drop = FALSE]),
  lacto_fraction = lacto_reads / total_reads,
  community      = ifelse(lacto_fraction >= 0.5, "lactobacillus", "anaerobe")
)

# The split point and the group sizes
sample_groups |>
  ggplot(aes(lacto_fraction)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Lactobacillus fraction of all microbial reads",
       y = "Number of samples",
       title = "Dashed line = the 0.5 split")
table(sample_groups$community)
```

Most samples sit near one end, which is the usual pattern: a vagina is
typically either Lactobacillus-dominated or dominated by anaerobes. Samples
near 0.5 are the ones where the label is a judgement call.

For context: is community type just another name for contraceptive arm?

```{r}
metadata |>
  left_join(sample_groups, by = "sample_id") |>
  with(table(arm, community))
```

## Step 2: check the sample order before any test

DESeq2 matches count columns to metadata rows by position only. If the orders
differ, it will run without complaining and every result will be wrong, so we
reorder to be sure rather than assume.

```{r}
meta <- as.data.frame(metadata)

# Gene IDs in the first column, raw counts (never CPM, never logged) after it
gene_ids <- gene_counts[[1]]
count_mat <- as.matrix(gene_counts[-1])
rownames(count_mat) <- gene_ids
storage.mode(count_mat) <- "integer"

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(gene_ids),
          !any(count_mat < 0),
          all(count_mat == floor(count_mat)))

# Reorder metadata rows to match the count columns, then prove they match
meta <- meta[match(colnames(count_mat), meta$sample_id), ]
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample_id

stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_mat), rownames(meta)))
stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_mat), sample_groups$sample_id))

# Attach the community labels and set the reference level.
# With "anaerobe" as reference, a POSITIVE log2FC means higher in "lactobacillus".
meta <- meta |>
  left_join(sample_groups, by = "sample_id")
meta$community <- factor(meta$community, levels = c("anaerobe", "lactobacillus"))
meta$rnaseq_batch <- factor(meta$rnaseq_batch)

table(meta$community)
```

## Step 3: the DESeq2 test

```{r}
# Sequencing batch goes into the design so it does not masquerade as biology
design_matrix <- model.matrix(~ rnaseq_batch + community, data = meta)
stopifnot(qr(design_matrix)$rank == ncol(design_matrix))

keep <- rowSums(count_mat) >= 10
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_mat[keep, ],
  colData = meta,
  design = ~ rnaseq_batch + community
)
dds <- DESeq(dds)

res <- results(dds, contrast = c("community", "lactobacillus", "anaerobe"),
               alpha = 0.05)

results_table <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") |>
  arrange(padj)

results_table |> filter(!is.na(padj)) |> slice_head(n = 20)
sum(results_table$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Step 4: check the direction of the contrast

The sign of `log2FoldChange` is a claim about which group has the higher mean.
Here is the independent check: count the reads per group directly and compare.

```{r}
norm <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)  # DESeq2's own normalised counts

dir_check <- results_table |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |> slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    mean_lactobacillus = rowMeans(norm[gene_id, meta$community == "lactobacillus", drop = FALSE]),
    mean_anaerobe = rowMeans(norm[gene_id, meta$community == "anaerobe", drop = FALSE]),
    higher_in = ifelse(mean_lactobacillus > mean_anaerobe, "lactobacillus", "anaerobe"),
    direction_agrees = (log2FoldChange > 0) == (mean_lactobacillus > mean_anaerobe)
  )
dir_check
all(dir_check$direction_agrees)
```

If `direction_agrees` is TRUE throughout, the sign of every fold change means
what we said: positive = higher in `lactobacillus`.

```{r}
# The single strongest gene, as a picture: each point is one sample
plotCounts(dds, gene = results_table$gene_id[1],
           intgroup = "community")
```

## Choices made

- Community groups defined from the **microbiome species table** (Lactobacillus
  fraction ≥ 0.5), then tested on the **gene table** — the alternative, using
  the metadata `bv` column, would label almost the same samples but is a
  clinical score, not a composition-based grouping.
- Split at 0.5 with no buffer zone, so samples near 0.5 get a firm label.
- *Lactobacillus* genus-level fraction (all Lactobacillus species); the
  alternative of *L. iners* + *L. crispatus* only would barely change the
  numbers because these two dominate the genus here.
- Reference level set to `anaerobe`, so positive log2FC = higher in
  `lactobacillus`; flipping the levels flips every sign but nothing else.
- `rnaseq_batch` in the design (alternative: ignoring batch, which risks
  calling batch effects biology).
- Genes with fewer than 10 raw reads across all samples dropped.
- Significance threshold: adjusted p (FDR) < 0.05; no fold-change cutoff, so
  small-but-consistent shifts are kept (alternative: also require
  |log2FC| ≥ 1).
- No samples dropped.
